description: Performance-management framework that translates strategy into objectives and measures across four perspectives, linked by cause-and-effect into a strategy map.
best_for: Defining engagement success criteria and target KPIs
Building the benefits-realisation tracker of a business case
Aligning C-level objectives with operational measures

dimensions.name: Financial
dimensions.description: How the organisation looks to shareholders / funders.
diagnostic_questions: Which financial outcome does the engagement move, and by how much?
Is the benefit cost reduction, revenue growth or capital efficiency?

dimensions.name: Customer
diagnostic_questions: Which customer outcome (time, quality, satisfaction) is the lead indicator?

dimensions.name: Internal Process
dimensions.description: The processes the organisation must excel at.
diagnostic_questions: Which process KPI drives the customer outcome?
What is its current baseline and variance?

dimensions.name: Learning & Growth
dimensions.description: Capabilities, culture and infrastructure needed to sustain improvement.
diagnostic_questions: Which capability gap blocks the process improvement?

pitfalls: Twenty KPIs per perspective — a scorecard nobody reads
No causal links between perspectives, so the map is a list, not a strategy
Only lagging (financial) indicators, no lead indicators
sources: Kaplan, R.S., Norton, D.P. — 'The Balanced Scorecard: Measures that Drive Performance', HBR (1992)
